answer: The node's global SSHv2 host keys (used by both server-side and client-side SSHv2 apps) are shown with 'show ssh-host-key-<public-key-algorithm> [public-key] [label] [fingerprint-algorithm] [fingerprint]'. There must be one host key per supported algorithm, so yes, more than one exists. The system auto-generates a host-key in the default DB, and additional host-keys can be added or overwritten via the ssh-keygen RPC. public-key-algorithm values: ecdsa-sha2-nistp256, ecdsa-sha2-nistp384, ecdsa-sha2-nistp521, ssh-rsa2048, ssh-rsa3072, ssh-rsa4096, ssh-ed25519 (ED25519 support starts in R9.0). public-key is PEM-encoded OpenSSH format, String 0..2048; label String 0..256; fingerprint-algorithm md5 or sha256; fingerprint String 0..95 as hex digit pairs. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. Use 'show ssh-host-key' for the whole list, or e.g. 'show ssh-host-key-ecdsa-sha2-nistp521' for one.

ssh-keygen generates an SSH private/public key pair and the existing keys in the system are replaced with the newly generated pair. Syntax: 'ssh-keygen [-b=<key-length>] [-l=<key-label>] [-t=<type>]', Operational mode only. -t is rsa, ecdsa or ed25519, default rsa. Key length via -b; if omitted the system uses the default for the key type. With secure mode disabled (security-policies/secure-mode): RSA supports 2048, 3072 or 4096 (default 2048); ECDSA supports 256, 384 or 521 (default 256). With secure mode enabled: RSA only 4096; ECDSA only 384 or 521 (default 384). ED25519 supports only 256 regardless of secure mode, and is available from R9.0. -l sets the key label; if not provided the label is the value of ne-id. Retrieve the resulting public key with 'show ssh-host-key'.

Add an SSHv2 known-hosts entry: 'add ssh-known-host-<id> address <value> public-key-algorithm <value> public-key <value> [label <value>]'. id is a unique name, String 0..64. address is the hostname, IPv4 or IPv6 address of the allowed/known peer host; IPv4 is dotted-quad and IPv6 uses RFC 5952 canonical text, and either may carry a zone index after a % sign (numeric form is canonical; if absent the device default zone is used). public-key-algorithm: ecdsa-sha2-nistp256, ecdsa-sha2-nistp384, ecdsa-sha2-nistp521, ssh-rsa2048, ssh-rsa3072, ssh-rsa4096, ssh-ed25519 (ED25519 from R9.0). public-key is the OpenSSH/PEM-format host public key, String 0..2048. label is String 0..256. 'set ssh-known-host-<id>' can only change label; 'show ssh-known-host-<id>' and 'delete ssh-known-host-<id>' also exist. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

The trusted-certificate object holds the X509v3 CA certificates (Root and Intermediate) trusted by the system. Syntax: 'set trusted-certificate[-id] [alarm-report-control <value>] [label <value>] [revocation-mode <value>]' and 'show trusted-certificate[-id]' with version, serial-number, subject-name, issuer, trust-chain, valid-from, valid-to, status, public-key-length, public-key-type, signature-key-type, signature-hash-algorithm, certificate-bytes, key-usage, extended-key-usage, modification-time, revocation-mode, alarm-report-control, label. revocation-mode is auto, force-revoked or force-unrevoked, default auto. alarm-report-control is allowed or inhibited, default allowed. label is String 0..256; id is string 0..4096; version is v3. Certificates are removed with the 'clear certificate' command, not with a delete on this object. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

Use 'terminate cable-id' (Operational Mode) to stop all running CableID verification tests. Because verification runs on a port-pair basis, the test can only be stopped after the current port-pair verification completes and before the next port-pair starts: the in-flight port-pair runs to completion, then the test exits. The maximum delay to terminate is therefore one port-pair verification time. The test is known to be terminated once cable-id-status cable-id-state changes to idle, so after issuing the command use 'show cable-id cable-id-status' to confirm the cable-id entity is back in the idle state. The show/terminate pair is documented under the cable-id command ('show cable-id', 'terminate cable-id'), which takes no parameters; show is also available in Candidate Configuration mode, terminate only in Operational Mode.

The CableID signal can only be sourced or terminated by the CAD10A and RD20TM cards; the signal is passed transparently in the OPSM. A CableID path starts at the end A port and terminates at the end Z port, where the signal is sourced/terminated, that is at a CAD10A DWDM port or an RD20TM ADE port. Accordingly, 'show cable-id-path-<name>' reports card-type-a and card-type-z with values RD20TM or CAD10A, plus port-a and port-z as port AIDs. The card type is derived from the provisioned fiber-connection at the port-A/port-Z attribute: when a fiber-connection is created, the CableID function checks whether it lands on a port of a CableID capable sled and, if so, captures that card type into the CableID path topology. In R8.0.1 the supported sleds are CAD10A and RD20TM.

Yes. cable-id-status is the container holding the process status and progress of a CableID-based fiber connection verification, and you are allowed to issue 'show cable-id cable-id-status' at any time to query progress. Syntax: 'show cable-id-status [cable-id-state] [test-progress]', available in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. cable-id-state values: idle (verification not running), running-incl-switching (running for both active and protected paths), running-no-switching (running only for the active path); default idle. test-progress is a string 0..255, default 'None', showing 'Not applicable' if cable-id-state is disabled, or 'N out of M completed' while running, where M is the total number of port-pairs to be tested and N the number already completed. Example output: cable-id-state idle, test-progress '1 out of 1 completed.'

Each carrier can discover up to one node. It is possible for multiple collocated carriers to discover the same node multiple times, each time connected to a different remote carrier. View the result with 'show carrier-neighbor-<local-carrier> [last-update] [age] [local-carrier-id] [ne-id] [ne-name] [ne-type] [remote-carrier-id] [ipv4-loopback-address] [ipv6-loopback-address]'. local-carrier is the local carrier instance that discovered the neighbor, string 0..16. ne-id and ne-name are string 0..256, ne-type string 0..64, remote-carrier-id string 0..64 and is the AID of the remote carrier connected to the local carrier, implying a specific remote port id. last-update is date-time YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ. The IPv4/IPv6 loopback addresses of the neighbor may be empty if not configured. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

Use 'show connection-ports-<degree-number>/<index> [port-name]', available in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. degree-number is uint16 in range 1..20 and must be greater than zero and not greater than max-degrees. index is uint32 in range 1..2 but is always 1 in the 1830 GX, since dwdm-line ports are bi-directional. port-name is an instance-identifier giving the dwdm-line port of the RD or ILAx card; as a consequence the OMS of the corresponding dwdm-port is created. Use 'show connection-ports*' to list all connection ports in the node, which returns rows such as connection-ports-1/1 with port-name port-1-3-dwdm-line1, or 'show connection-ports-5/1' for a single degree, which returns just the port-name (for example port-4-1-dwdm-line1).

Use the custom-tlv command, which shows the list of Organizational Specific TLV (Type-Length-Value) parameter information. Syntax: 'show custom-tlv-<lldp-port>/<direction>/<oui>/<subtype> [value]', available in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. lldp-port is the local port associated with the LLDP agent, string 0..64. direction is ingress or egress. oui is the Organization Unique Identifier of the TLV, a hexadecimal representation of the 24 bit identifier, string 1..6. subtype is the sub-type identifier of the TLV within the scope of that OUI, string 1..507. The value attribute carries the TLV content.

No. The external-fiber-connection is set autonomously by TNMS; although it is possible to configure it manually, it is not recommended to do so. It is the physical link representation of a connection between two ports of L0 cards in different NEs, or in the same NE in disaggregated configurations. Syntax: 'add external-fiber-connection-<name> src-port-name <value> dst-port-name <value> [label] [scope] [src-node-id] [src-card-name] [dst-node-id] [dst-card-name] [fiber-connection-type]'. Before R8.0 the user also had to set port external-connectivity to yes. From R8.0, with l0-mode-op set to slte, external fiber connections can represent intra-NE connections between RD20TM ADE ports or between CAD10A DWDM and RD20TM ADE ports; those entries must have scope set to cable-id (values general-purpose or cable-id, default general-purpose).

A fiber-connection is the physical link representation of a connection between two distinct ports (or two distinct sub-ports) in the same NE, in an OADM/ILA topology. An external-fiber-connection represents a connection between two ports of L0 cards in different NEs, or in the same NE in disaggregated configurations, and it is set autonomously by TNMS (manual configuration is possible but not recommended). fiber-connection takes name (String 0..64), label (0..256), src-port and dst-port as instance identifiers, and fiber-connection-type one-way or two-way, default two-way. external-fiber-connection instead identifies endpoints by string: src-node-id and dst-node-id (0..256, logically the ne-name), src-card-name/dst-card-name (0..64), src-port-name/dst-port-name (0..128), and adds the scope attribute (general-purpose or cable-id, default general-purpose).

Yes. icdp is the Nokia Carrier Discovery Protocol, and its global-switch flag, which enables icdp, has values true or false with a default of true. Syntax: 'set icdp global-switch <true|false>' and 'show icdp [global-switch]', both available in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. The icdp object is managed by the system and cannot be manually deleted. Example: 'set icdp global-switch true' enables icdp. The related discovery results are viewed with the carrier-neighbor command, where each carrier can discover up to one node.

INCI is the Inter-NE Communication Interface, part of the Inter NE inter-op feature. It provides an API-based communication infrastructure for control plane communication across different network elements, for example between a transponder such as CHM6 on 1830 GX G40 and a line system such as FLEXILS, using gRPC server/client as the core mechanism. When the INCI service is enabled the gRPC server is started and bound to the local IP address; when an INCI neighbor instance is configured, gRPC client sessions are established. It is not running by default: 'set inci [inci-enabled <true|false>]' with inci-enabled defaulting to false. Enable it with 'set inci inci-enabled true' and check with 'show inci [inci-enabled]'. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

Compare the provisioned name against the name the remote NE reports. On 'add inci-neighbor-<neighbor-id> neighbor-address <value> configured-node-name <value> [alarm-report-control <allowed|inhibited>]', configured-node-name is the user provisioned name of the remote NE and is used to compare against the discovered-node-name, which is the name of the remote NE as sent by the remote NE. Both are string 0..128. 'show inci-neighbor-<neighbor-id>' also returns discovered-node-id, the node ID of the remote node as received from it (string 0..12), plus neighbor-address, neighbor-port, connection-status, alarm-report-control and oper-state (enabled or disabled). neighbor-id is the node-ID AID of the provisioned neighbor; alarm-report-control defaults to inhibited. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

Both timers are attributes of interface-neighbor: 'set interface-neighbor-<local-interface> [discovery-cycle-time <value>] [discovery-timeout <value>] [discovery-enabled <value>] [alarm-report-control <value>] [label <value>]'. discovery-cycle-time is the periodicity at which sndp discover messages are sent, range 30..300 seconds, default 30. discovery-timeout is the time after which discovery is considered failed; when it occurs, neighbor-adjacency-state transitions to blackout. Its range is 300..1800 seconds, default 300. discovery-enabled turns discovery on or off on the local interface, true or false, default true. neighbor-adjacency-state values are blackout, discovery, holding, unknown, default unknown; oper-state is enabled or disabled, default disabled. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

No. The links container within the topology is dynamically filled in by the system, allowing the NCT topology to be derived and displayed. The command is simply 'show links', with no parameters, available in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. The related nct-connection command works the same way: it shows existing links between NCT ports in a multi-chassis NE and those links are also dynamically filled in by the system. Existing topology neighbor information can be removed manually with the 'clear topology' command.

The lldp object carries a single attribute, hold-on-timer, which is the time to keep neighbor information in case the neighbor does not send an explicit Time-To-Live (TTL) TLV. It is a number of seconds and defaults to 900. Syntax: 'set lldp [hold-on-timer <value>]' and 'show lldp [hold-on-timer]', both in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. The lldp object is managed by the system and cannot be manually deleted. Example: 'set lldp hold-on-timer 60'. On a per-neighbor basis, 'show lldp-neighbor' reports ttl, the number of seconds until the remote system information expires; if the remote system does not provide a ttl value, that parameter is set to the global hold-on-timer.

'show lldp-local-info-<lldp-port> [chassis-id-subtype] [chassis-id] [port-id-subtype] [port-id] [port-description] [system-name] [system-description] [supported-capabilities] [enabled-capabilities]' shows the LLDP local system information sent on an lldp-port. On the 1830 GX: chassis-id-subtype is chassis-component and chassis-id is the chassis serial number; port-id-subtype is local and port-id is the port AID; port-description is the port name; system-name is the NE name; and system-description is the string 'Nokia Corporation.Converged OS, Version <release id> _ build <software label>'. supported-capabilities and enabled-capabilities take the values router and bridge. All string attributes are 0..255. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. Examples: 'show lldp-local-info' or 'show lldp-local-info-comm-eth-1-11-ETH4'.

No, the egress direction is not supported. 'show lldp-neighbor-<lldp-port>/<direction>' takes direction as the direction in which the neighbor was detected, and the only value is ingress, for example 'show -r lldp-neighbor-ethernet-1-1-3/ingress' or 'show -r lldp-neighbor-comm-eth-1-11-ETH4/ingress'. The same restriction applies to lldp-port-statistics, whose direction is also ingress only. The lldp-neighbor information is kept indefinitely, until the port is decommissioned or the data is manually cleared by the user. Available attributes include last-update, age, chassis-id-subtype/chassis-id, port-id-subtype/port-id, port-description, system-name, system-description, supported-capabilities, enabled-capabilities and ttl. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

No. All counter values in an lldp-port-statistics entry are maintained on a continuing basis and are not deleted upon expiration of the TTL timing counters associated with the LLDP neighbor information. The only thing that stops them is administrative state: all statistical counters associated with a particular port on the local LLDP agent become frozen whenever lldp-admin-status is disabled for that port. Syntax: 'show lldp-port-statistics-<lldp-port>/<direction> [last-change-time] [last-clear-time] [total-ageouts] [total-discarded-frames] [error-frames] [total-frames-in] [total-frames-out] [total-discarded-tlvs] [total-unrecognized-tlvs]'; direction is ingress only, egress is not supported. total-ageout counts the times a neighbor's information was deleted from the lldp-neighbor list due to TTL expiry. Counters default to 0; last-clear-time defaults to 0000-01-01T00:00:00Z.

Use 'show nct-connection-<src-port>/<dst-port> [src-chassis] [dst-chassis] [src-chassis-state] [dst-chassis-state]', which shows NCT connectivity information, that is the existing links between NCT ports in a multi-chassis NE. These links are dynamically filled in by the system, allowing the NCT topology to be derived and displayed. src-chassis-state and dst-chassis-state take the values node controller, provisioned and unprovisioned. src-port and dst-port must be NCT ports: for a commissioned chassis they are the port AID, and for an unprovisioned chassis they take the format '<chassis-serial-number>-<slot>-NCT-<id>'. Similarly src-chassis and dst-chassis are the chassis AID if commissioned, or the chassis serial number if unprovisioned. All are string 0..64. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

The sndp command has a single attribute, sndp-enabled, which is the switch controlling the sndp feature. Values are true or false, with a default of true, so the feature is on unless disabled. Syntax: 'set sndp [sndp-enabled <value>]' and 'show sndp [sndp-enabled]', both available in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. Example: 'show sndp sndp-enabled'. The related per-interface control is interface-neighbor, whose discovery-cycle-time attribute sets the periodicity at which sndp discover messages are sent (30..300 seconds, default 30) and whose discovery-enabled switch turns discovery on or off on a given local interface.

'add submarine-link-<name> src-node-id <value> src-port-name <value> dst-node-id <value> dst-port-name <value> degree-target-tx-power <value> [...]'. The mandatory attributes are src-node-id and dst-node-id (the NE names of the endpoint nodes, String 0..256), src-port-name and dst-port-name (the OTS dwdm-line port of the degree, String 0..128), and degree-target-tx-power, the target launch power at the ROADM into the primary fiber. fiber-length is the fiber length in km of the associated fiber pair ID, decimal64 in range 0..25000 km, default 0, and does not include the length of branch segments. Optional attributes include label, src/dst-card-name (0..64), link-name, fiber-pair-id, segment-list (0..512), bu-segment-index (uint16, default 0), rx/tx-fiber-type, gsnr in dB, degree-expected-rx-power, commissioning-snr-margin, launch-condition (flat-tx or pfib, default pfib), allocated-spectrum-list (start/end frequency pairs, max 32 elements), and fiber-connection-type, which is two-way only for submarine links (default two-way).

supporting-fiber-connection shows the list of fiber connections supporting a given entity. Syntax: 'show supporting-fiber-connection-<name> [fiber-connection-list]', available in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. name is the name of the entity, String 0..64, and fiber-connection-list is an instance-identifier giving the supported fiber connection path. It is used by CableID: 'show -r cable-id-path-<name>' displays the supporting-fiber-connection container and its fiber-connection-list along with all the cable-id-path parameters for the port-pair, for example 'supporting-fiber-connection-1-6-ade6-1-8-ade6' with fiber-connection-list 'supporting-fiber-connection-R1'.
